speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your symptoms of a longstanding pruritic rash and numbness/tingling in your palms. To differentiate between conditions like diabetic neuropathy, leprosy, or a contact dermatitis, could you please describe the specific appearance of the rash and whether you have any history of diabetes or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the combination of an itchy rash on the upper body and face with sensory changes in the palms, alongside exposure to rice farming and livestock, is highly suggestive of a specific systemic infection. To confirm this, please tell me: do you notice any hair loss, thickened skin on your fingers or earlobes, or any eye irritation? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential. REQUEST TEST: Serum Nerve Conduction Study (NCS).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Chronic inflammatory cells with features suggestive of leprosy. Nerve_Conduction_Studies: Reduced sensory nerve action potentials in the ulnar nerves. Serology: Anti-PGL-1_antibodies: Positive. Vital_Signs: Temperature: 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure: 130/85 mmHg, Heart_Rate: 72 bpm, Respiratory_Rate: 14 breaths/min. Skin_Examination: Observation: Multiple erythematous macules and papules on the face, arms, chest, and back. Hypopigmented macules around the elbows. Palpation: Insensitivity to light touch, temperature, and pinprick around the hypopigmented areas. Slight reduction in grip strength bilaterally. Special_Tests: Loss of eyebrow and eyelash hairs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Leprosy (Hansen's Disease). The biopsy showing chronic inflammation with leprosy features, positive Anti-PGL-1 antibodies, loss of eyebrow/eyelash hairs, and sensory loss over hypopigmented patches with ulnar nerve involvement are all pathognomonic for this condition.
